definitions.type: ℕ → real finite dimensional inner product spaces
definitions.definition: Ambient(m)=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), the space of m real coordinates with norm ‖x‖₂=(Σ_{j<m}|x_j|²)^(1/2). The sum is zero when m=0. Distances are norms of differences. More generally the native EuclideanSpace k (Fin m), for a real-or-complex-like field k, is the m-coordinate k-space with this same sum-of-squared-absolute-values norm; its scalar vector-space structure is coordinatewise.

binders.type: vector in the indicated real or k-valued coordinate space

definitions.definition: ofReal(v) is max(v,0) embedded in the extended nonnegative reals. The notation z.toReal for z∈[0,∞] is its real value when finite, and zero for z=∞.

definitions.type: real exponent × subset of a Borel extended metric space → [0,∞]
definitions.definition: H^u(B)=μH[u](B) denotes Mathlib's unnormalized Hausdorff measure, the metric measure mkMetric for the gauge r↦r^u on the Borel sigma algebra. The metric-measure construction takes countable-cover outer contents for this gauge, with the empty-set gauge cost forced to zero, and their supremum as the scale tends to zero. Its precise cover evaluation will be applied as an explicit native source, rather than assumed as an extra premise. No spherical or dimensional normalization factor is used.

binders.type: subset of a Borel extended metric space

definitions.type: subset of an extended metric space → [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For B in an extended metric space, equipped with its Borel measurable structure when computing H, dimH(B)=sup{d∈[0,∞): H^d(B)=∞}, the supremum taken in [0,∞] and with sup ∅=0. This is native Mathlib dimH. Positive-exponent critical-exponent directions are invoked as explicit native sources. We use no zero-exponent measure assertion.

binders.type: subset of an extended metric space

definitions.definition: I=[0,1]={t∈ℝ:0≤t≤1}. This is unitInterval in the basis header.

For a metric space Z, MaxProd(Z)=Z×ℝ with distance d_max((x,t),(y,u))=max(d_Z(x,y),|t−u|). For B⊆Z, B×I always denotes a subset of MaxProd(Z) in intermediate lemmas. All metric spaces in integration or Hausdorff-measure statements carry their Borel sigma algebra.

appendCoord(m)(x,t) is the vector whose first m coordinates are those of x and whose last coordinate is t. In the exact basis header it is WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.lastCases t (fun j => x j)). Its target always carries the Euclidean norm; its source here carries the maximum metric. It is a total coordinate construction, including m=0. Under the problem's identification ℝ^n×ℝ=ℝ^(n+1), the Euclidean set E×[0,1] is appendCoord(n) '' (E×I).

definitions.type: nonnegative real × map of pseudo extended metric spaces → propositions
definitions.definition: LipschitzWith(K,f) means ∀x,y, edist(f x,f y)≤K·edist(x,y), where K is a finite nonnegative real embedded into [0,∞]. On metric spaces this is the usual distance inequality.

binders.type: map between pseudo extended metric spaces

definitions.type: nonnegative real × map of extended metric spaces → propositions
definitions.definition: AntilipschitzWith(L,f) means ∀x,y, edist(x,y)≤L·edist(f x,f y), with finite L≥0. On metric spaces this is the corresponding ordinary distance inequality.

definitions.type: real or extended nonnegative base × real exponent → corresponding scalars
definitions.definition: The notation v^u uses the standard real power; on positive real v it is exp(u log v), with 0^u=0 for u>0 and 0^0=1. For extended nonnegative bases it is the usual extension: at u>0, ∞^u=∞ and 0^u=0; at u=0 the value is 1; at u<0, 0^u=∞ and ∞^u=0. Only nonnegative real bases and positive exponents occur in the covering calculations. The native real function at negative v is defined using |v|, as in Real.rpow.

inputs.statement: For every metric space X and nonempty A⊆X with dimH(A)≠∞, the maximum product metric satisfies dimH(A×I)=dimH(A)+1 in [0,∞], and dimH(A×I)≠∞. Thus the corresponding finite real dimensions satisfy the same equality. No compactness or positive-dimension assumption is required.

The map appendCoord(n):MaxProd(Ambient n)→Ambient(n+1) is bijective and, for all p,p′ in its source, d_max(p,p′)≤d₂(appendCoord(n)p,appendCoord(n)p′)≤√2·d_max(p,p′). Thus it is √2-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz, and for every subset S⊆MaxProd(Ambient n), dimH(appendCoord(n) '' S)=dimH(S). Constants are independent of n and E. This includes n=0.

output.statement: With the stipulated Euclidean metrics and identification ℝ^n×ℝ=ℝ^(n+1), dimH(E×[0,1])=dimH(E)+1; equivalently dimH(appendCoord(n) '' (E×I))=dimH(E)+1. Both dimensions are finite, so this is also the equality of their real values.

argument.text: Return to the original natural n and E⊆Ambient n. H001 gives that E is nonempty. N004 gives dimH E≤n and dimH E≠∞, including n=0. Instantiate N105 with X=Ambient n and A=E. Its nonemptiness and finite-dimension conditions are exactly these two available facts. It yields dimH(E×I)=dimH E+1 in MaxProd(Ambient n), and finiteness of that product dimension. Now apply N106 to the subset E×I. Under the fixed coordinate identification, appendCoord(n) '' (E×I) is precisely the original E×[0,1] in Euclidean ℝ^(n+1): its first n coordinates belong to E and its last coordinate belongs to [0,1], and conversely every such vector has this preimage. N106 transfers the maximum-metric dimension to this Euclidean image. Therefore dimH(E×[0,1])=dimH E+1 with the stipulated Euclidean metric. Both sides are finite by N004 and N105, so their [0,∞] equality is the equality of finite real dimensions as well. This proves P. The original compactness hypothesis remains retained but is unused in this strengthened basis route.
